canonical_claim: An EBR (Epoch-Based Reclamation) GC core -- writers holding a pin epoch (an ephemeral Keeper node), GC advancing through safe_epoch/commit_epoch/birth_epoch and waiting for quiescence, with generations on blob keys (blobs/<H>/<g>) as the ABA guard -- was rejected because a stuck or wedged writer held down safe_epoch and stalled reclamation of all dropped parts across all writers, Keeper was required for correctness, and a long-running INSERT could delay GC for its entire duration. It was replaced by the incarnation-token design, where regular GC candidates are restricted to journal-known nodes so fresh uploads are structurally invisible and can never be candidates, and a wedged writer has no pin to hold down.
